title: Molecular communication laboratory and testbed
summary: Creation of an operational laboratory and experimental platform combining chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics, signal processing and machine learning to validate molecular communication theories.

sections.title: Laboratory creation
paragraphs: The project was carried out at King’s College London as part of a Postdoctoral Research Associate position presented publicly as an R&D Project Manager role.
items: Identification and preparation of the premises.
Selection and ordering of equipment, fume hoods, heavy equipment and consumables.
Definition of safety and operating procedures.
Training teams in the use of the laboratory.

sections.title: Experimental platform
paragraphs: The operational testbed enabled the experimental validation of molecular communication theories using chemical reactions to process signals.
items: Study of filtering, saturation, amplification and encoding functions.
Design of a system combining chemistry, microfluidics, UV-Visible detection, electronics and software.
Management of a team averaging five people: one junior PDRA, two doctoral researchers and two Master’s interns.
Training of nine people in total.

sections.title: Funding and project management
paragraphs: Two EPSRC grants of €300,000 and €60,000, totalling €360,000, were managed as part of the project.
items: Partial contribution to the first funding application.
Complete drafting of the second funding application.

sections.title: Artificial intelligence and signal analysis
paragraphs: A one-dimensional convolutional neural network was developed to analyse UV-Visible signals and estimate the molecular composition and concentrations of aqueous solutions.
items: Development using Python, TensorFlow and scikit-learn.
Preparation and analysis of experimental signals.
Work published in IEEE Transactions on Molecular, Biological and Multi-Scale Communications in 2026.

sections.title: Open-source syringe pumps
paragraphs: Six syringe pumps were designed and manufactured for integration into the experimental platform.
items: Development of control software in C++ and Python.

sections.title: Results
paragraphs: The laboratory was created, the experimental testbed was made operational, and the work resulted in two publications for which I was the first author and principal writer.
items: Real-time signal processing via chemical reactions for a microfluidic molecular communication system — Nature Communications, 2023.
CNN-Based Detection of Mixed-Molecule Concentrations in Molecular Communication — IEEE T-MBMC, 2026.
